facts.statement: Property is 18 Brindlewick Row, Vellmere, ZZ1 1ZZ; tenant Iris Bell reported heating failure on 6 May 2025, thermostat blank, hot water available via immersion.
No leak, unusual smell or warning light reported; report falls in May, outside the rulebook's cold months (10-4), and no occupant vulnerability is disclosed — classified routine, not an emergency.
Hearthline Heating attended 7 May, found a failed control board and restored heating by resetting the unit; estimate £460 plus VAT for replacement; no job sheet attached.

Landlord Jonas Reed approved the £95 plus VAT diagnostic only and required contact before any repair authorisation; on 8 May he declined to approve the £460 plus VAT repair pending a clearer breakdown and written attendance record.
Invoice NBL-005-INV-71 dated 12 May, £95 + £19 VAT = £114, for diagnostic attendance on 7 May, remittance 00-00-00 / 00000000, due 19 May.
On 13 May the contractor emailed asking that payment be made to 11-11-11 / 11111111 instead, offering a revised invoice, with no independent verification information.
No payment instruction has been entered on the file, and the quoted repair remains unapproved.
Contractor states the reset is not a permanent repair and the fault could recur; he has not given an expected duration and has not supplied the job sheet despite requests on 7 and 9 May.
Access on 7 May was by tenant consent; the door buzzer is unreliable and callers must phone on arrival. No management key was issued.
